benchmark: Eight-worker complete-match rollout: eager vs torch.compile CPU inference
finding: The single-state torch.compile advantage did not transfer to rollout workers. Cold eight-worker complete-match throughput fell from 13.15 to 4.30 games/s; measured policy inference rose from about 65.8 to 944.6 ms/match and peak RSS rose from 6.60 to 11.67 GiB. Keep compilation disabled for training. This small run is a speed comparison, not a strength evaluation.
limitations: Each condition ran 64 matches and included process startup and compilation. Same seeds and episode offsets were used; policy action sampling and game randomness mean match outcomes are not a powered strength comparison. Test set was a short Max Damage workload, not the full opponent mixture.
